name: Moped
description: A device with fully operative pedals, an automatic transmission and a motor producing no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,492 W), with a maximum design speed of 30 mph on level ground. It isn't a motor vehicle, so it needs no title, registration or insurance, but its rider needs an operator's license. Defined by Nebraska Revised Statutes §60-637 and regulated by §§60-6,309 to 60-6,313.
restrictions: Fully operative pedals and an automatic transmission
Its motor produces no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,492 W) and has a maximum design speed of 30 mph on level ground; the definition also caps the motor's cylinder capacity at 50 cc
Riders need a valid operator's license, but not a Class M motorcycle license
Riders and passengers must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting FMVSS 218; the exemption for riders 21 and older applies only to Class M license holders who completed a motorcycle safety course
Riders need eye protection (glasses, goggles or a face shield) or a windshield
Exempt from the title, registration and safety responsibility (insurance) laws
Gets full use of a lane on highways posted 45 mph or less; on faster ones it keeps to the right in single file
Never on interstate highways or sidewalks
Carries a passenger only if designed for one, and its handlebars sit no more than 15 inches above their mount
